Context: StarRocks-on-Sirius (GPU SQL engine embedded in a StarRocks compute node, "CN"). An SF1000 profiling campaign found four blockers; you are helping choose the best fix for one of them.
Read first: /home/prestouser/.claude/plans/sf1000-top4-fixes-plan.md (the plan: issues, candidate solutions, criteria, acceptance tests) and the relevant findings in /home/prestouser/.claude/plans/starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-planning-cardinality-backpressure.md (sections 3B, 3C, 4). Evidence bundle: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000 (WORKFLOW-PLAN.md indexes it; cn1-cnlog.txt, cn1-quent.txt, card-compare-*.txt, cn1/engine-cn0.log, cn1/dump/ are the raw material).
Source tree (read-only for you): /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf (engine C++ under src/, CN Rust under experimental/starrocks/src, translator under experimental/starrocks/crates/starrocks-plan-translator, StarRocks FE Java under experimental/starrocks/starrocks/fe, engine docs under docs/super-sirius/).
Rules: do not modify the source tree, do not start clusters or GPU jobs, write only under /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/. Distinguish measured facts from inference. Cite file:line for every mechanism you rely on.

Four specs were written: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/oom-failfast-SPEC.md, /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/parked-bookkeeping-SPEC.md, /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/files-cardinality-SPEC.md, /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/fragment-fusion-SPEC.md. Read all four. Check them for interactions and contradictions (fail-fast error handling vs the bookkeeping's Err-path expectations; fusion vs spill vs FE cardinalities: which of the six failing queries each rescues and whether two fixes fight; shared files edited by two specs; test suites that would collide). Write /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/INTEGRATION.md with: the build/landing order, the shared-file conflicts to expect, the combined SF1000 verification matrix (which arm proves which spec, in which order, with pass criteria), and any spec that must change (edit that spec file in place and say what you changed). Return a short summary.

- ooc-sort-dev: Use when developing, building, testing, or iterating on the disk-backed (out-of-core) sort implementation for cudf-polars in ~/bzaitlen/test-data/ooc-sort/. Covers installing into the rapidsmpf container env, running streaming sort tests, and the phase-by-phase implementation workflow.
- build-errors: Use this skill when the build fails, compilation errors occur, or you see undefined references, linker errors, CUDA compilation issues, missing headers, or template instantiation failures. Analyzes errors, suggests fixes, and iteratively rebuilds until success.
- build-sirius-starrocks: Build the Sirius-as-StarRocks-CN stack on a fresh GPU box — UCX, nixl, libsirius, StarRocks FE, and the Rust CN. Use when standing the stack up from scratch, recovering a broken toolchain (g++/ld/nvml shims, CUDA 13, no-root conda deps), applying the StarRocks proto patch, or relocating pixi/cargo/Maven onto local NVMe.
- cn-tuning: Size Sirius StarRocks CN memory and operator budgets for a given GPU box and TPC-H scale factor. Use when choosing GPU_MEM, STAGING, HOST_MEM, hash_partition_bytes, scan_task_batch_size, or when a query OOMs / exhausts the exchange arena / looks like an engine bug that is actually mis-sizing. Covers the derived-flag path vs a full sirius.yaml.
- dataset-manager: Use this skill to generate benchmark datasets (TPC-H, TPC-DS, etc.). Trigger when the user needs test data at a specific scale factor for benchmarking or testing. Supports parquet and duckdb output formats.
- log-analyzer: Use this skill to analyze Sirius query execution logs — to find why a query is slow, diagnose validation errors (wrong results), spot excessive downgrading, identify pipeline gaps, or compare two runs of the same query. Trigger whenever the user mentions a Sirius log file, says "look at this log", asks about per-operator time, pipeline gaps, memory pressure, downgrade behavior, validation/correctness mismatches, or wants to compare two query runs. Also use as a hand-off target from race-check (for two-run comparisons), runtime-errors (for "where did the query stall before hang"), and validate (for diffing the bad run against a good run). This is the log-only counterpart to profile-analyzer (nsys) and optimization-advisor (source-level guidance).
- module-context: Automatically identify which dependency library modules are relevant to a task and load their API documentation into context. Use PROACTIVELY before implementing features, fixing bugs, or writing new operators — analyzes the task description and loads cudf, rmm, duckdb, cucascade module docs to improve code quality. Trigger when the user asks to implement, add, fix, or modify GPU operators, pipeline components, memory management, joins, aggregations, sorting, expressions, or data I/O.
- module-discover: Discover and document a dependency library or submodule — analyzes all uses within the codebase, divides the library into logical modules, identifies which modules are used, and generates LLM-consumable API documentation for each module. Use when the user wants to understand a library dependency, map its modules, or generate API reference docs for a submodule.
- optimization-advisor: Use this skill to find exactly which source code to optimize for better GPU performance. Maps nsys profile hotspots to specific Sirius source files and functions, classifies bottlenecks as GPU-bound, CPU-bound, or sync-bound, and recommends actionable code changes. Trigger when the user wants to know what to optimize, where to focus coding effort, or wants source-level optimization guidance. This skill focuses on actionable source code targets — for generating performance reports and measurements, use profile-analyzer instead.
- pr-digest: Generates a "learning" PR-review digest — a markdown file at PR_digests/PR_digest_<N>.md that explains what a GitHub PR does, why, and exactly where in the code, with clickable file/line links and trimmed diffs. Use this whenever the user shares a GitHub PR URL (e.g. github.com/owner/repo/pull/1234) and wants to understand, summarize, review, walk through, or get up to speed on what changed — phrases like "can you review this PR", "what does this PR do", "help me understand this pull request", "summarize the changes in PR
- pre-commit-cleanup: Clean the current Git changes before committing. Use when preparing to commit or when the pre-commit cleanliness hook blocks a commit.
- profile-analyzer: Use this skill to understand why a Sirius query is slow, identify GPU bottlenecks, or detect performance regressions. Generates reports with kernel occupancy, memory bandwidth, operator attribution, and cross-run comparisons. Trigger when the user mentions profiling, nsys, GPU utilization, kernel analysis, performance reports, or wants to compare query timings across runs. This skill focuses on measurement and reporting — for mapping hotspots to source code fixes, use optimization-advisor instead.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- tpch-2host: Bring up Sirius StarRocks CNs across two physical GB200 hosts with nixl over cross-host NVLink, and the matching stock StarRocks (engine B) two-machine baseline. Use when replicating the two-host experiment, setting SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_ARENA=fabric, debugging a 0.4 GB/s cuda_ipc fallback, or running engine B as 1 FE + 1 BE per host.
- tpch-bench: Operate the Sirius-as-StarRocks-CN demo and its TPC-H benchmark on the 4x GB200 box. Use when bringing the multi-GPU (N-CN, one CN per GPU) cluster up or down, running a query or the 22-query sweep, verifying the nixl/NVLink transport, triaging a failing/hanging/slow query, checking results against DuckDB, or reproducing the A-vs-B comparison against stock StarRocks.
- tpch-cn-sweep: Run the 22-query TPC-H sweep against a Sirius StarRocks CN cluster on any box, scale factor, data path, or GPU count. Use when launching bench.sh, sizing GPU_MEM/STAGING, checking results against the DuckDB oracle, or triaging pass/wedge/refused rows. Not the in-process Sirius-vs-DuckDB benchmark skill; not the GB200-hardcoded tpch-bench ops skill.
- update-docs: Use this skill to update Super Sirius documentation after code changes. Trigger when the user says "update docs", "refresh documentation", "sync docs with code changes", or after merging PRs that changed the Super Sirius codebase. Inspects merged PRs since the last update and patches affected doc files.

Claude should use this skill whenever asked to write some sort of internal communications (status reports, leadership updates, 3P updates, company newsletters, FAQs, incident reports, project updates, etc.).
- anthropic-skills:learn: Use this skill when the user wants intellectual understanding — learning how or why something works, not getting a task done or soliciting Claude's judgment.

Trigger for:
- Explicit learning requests: teach, explain, ELI5, walk me through, quiz me, flashcards, "I'm rusty on"; definitions ("what is X")
- Terse concept names implying "help me understand this": "Galois theory," "transformers, from scratch"
- Confusion signals: "won't stick," "keep mixing these up," "not getting it"
- Learning-path questions: prerequisites, sequencing, what to study before X
- Conceptual questions about mechanisms, causes, or dynamics

Don't trigger for:
- Tasks: coding, writing, calculation, translation, factual lookup, news updates
- Personal troubleshooting; resource/textbook recommendations
- Claude's evaluative verdict: opinion prompts ("do you think X", "settle this", "honest take", "is X dead / still taken seriously") and interpretive takes ("was X really as harsh as people say")

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

# SF1000 profiling: planning / cardinality / backpressure — evidence bundle and analysis plan

Build: worktree /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf, branch perf/profile-sf1000 = d24f02c4 + 85658f09 (aggregate gate) +
9a5a4da6 (async sender dispatch) + 45dab3be (Quent probes: scan_split_read, stream hops, staging leases, CN fragment labels).
Data: /scratch/sirius/datasets/tpch_sf1000 (decimal TPC-H, one parquet dir per table). Queries: experimental/starrocks/benchmarks/tpch/queries/qNN.sql.

## Evidence (scratchpad = /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000)
- survey/explain/qNN.costs.txt, qNN.verbose.txt   FE EXPLAIN COSTS / VERBOSE for all 22 queries (fragments, join distribution, cardinality: 1 everywhere)
- survey/plan-summary.txt                          explain_summary.py over all 22 (joins with build/probe children and broadcast tables)
- cn1/  cn4/  standalone/                           the three arms; each has runs/runs.csv (query,run,phase,status,ms,rows,start_utc), runs/qNN.rK.out(.err)
- cn1/cluster.log, cn4/cluster.log                  FE + CN logs (fragment run started/finished, declared input stream cardinality, relayed batches, transmitted batches via nixl, OOM reschedule warnings)
- cn1/dump/fragment-*.txt, plan-*.substrait         every fragment the FE sent to the 1-CN and the translator's Substrait plan
- cn1/quent/.cnN/<session>/, cn4/quent/.cnN/<session>/, standalone/quent/<session>/   Quent ndjson (task FSM, data_batch, batch_placement, memory, scan_split_read)
- standalone/runs/qNN.explain.txt                   DuckDB/Sirius EXPLAIN of the same SQL (the stats-aware planner's choice)
- <arm>-cnlog.json (cnlog_extract.py), <arm>-quent.txt / .json (quent_bp.py), card-compare-<arm>.txt (card_compare.py), results.md (results_table.py)
- ../../oracle/tpch_sf1000/qNN.tsv                  DuckDB CPU oracle answers; compare-*.txt

## Tools (same dir)
explain_summary.py, cnlog_extract.py, card_compare.py, quent_bp.py, results_table.py, ../quent_summary.py (per-operator Computing sums)

## Facts established before the analysis
1. FE StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode sets outputRowCount = 1 for FILES() scans ("we don't know the real schema in file, just use the default Row Count now"); every column statistic UNKNOWN. Hence every plan node has cardinality 1 and the CBO picks BROADCAST for most joins (orders 1.5B rows broadcast in q07/q09/q10..., lineitem 3.79B rows as the build side of q04's LEFT SEMI JOIN, partsupp 800M in q02).
2. Engine stream ids == FE exchange node ids; the receiver declares the exact parked row count per stream before build() ("declared input stream cardinality"), so DuckDB plans the receiver fragment with exact input cardinalities, but only after every sender finished (receiver-first rendezvous, local_exchange.rs). Nothing streams across a fragment boundary: the whole intermediate is parked on the GPU.
3. Engine OOM handling: gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp reschedules a task on OOM up to MAX_RETRIES=100 with a 50 ms sleep, then fails the query ("exceeded maximum retry limit"). It does not wait for memory to be released and cannot spill parked batches. q05 and q08 died this way on 1 CN at SF1000 (GPU_SCAN OOM, 101 s and 168 s).
4. Reserving.requested_bytes / peak_estimate vs Computing.peak_allocated_bytes (Quent task FSM) measure the engine's own memory estimation; standalone SF10 q01 requested 20.8 GB for a 5.6 GB peak.

## Analysis dimensions (workflow)
A. Planning: per query, FE fragment tree and join distribution vs the DuckDB/Sirius standalone plan; what a stats-aware FE would choose; where the translator/CN could override (e.g. swap build/probe, refuse broadcast above a row threshold, local re-planning of a broadcast join once the actual parked cardinality is known).
B. Cardinality: FE estimate vs actual rows per exchange (card_compare), engine reservation estimate vs peak (quent_bp), the receiver-first exact-cardinality mechanism and its cost.
C. Backpressure: parked bytes and dwell per fragment, staging lease held/in-transit time and max concurrency vs SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES, Reserving/Queued waits, OOM reschedule storms, nixl transmit lease_ms/write_ms, 1-CN vs 4-CN scaling per query, standalone vs CN.
Each per-query analysis is verified adversarially (two skeptics with different lenses); the synthesis ranks findings with the evidence lines and proposes changes with file paths and confidence.

## Facts added after the 1-CN sweep (13:19 UTC)
5. Supported on the CN path at SF1000 (1 CN, 100 GiB pool): q01 q02 q03 q04 q06 q07 q10 q11 q12 q13 q14 q15 q19 q20 q22 pass (15). Fail: q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 = OOM at GPU_SCAN after 100 reschedules

18	## Candidate solutions to weigh (input to the design workflow, not the decision)
19	
20	1. **Fail fast.** (a) Abort at the reservation gate when `retry_count > 0 && freed == 0 && retry floor > grant`; (b) abort in the reschedule path when downgrade freed 0 and pool usage == limit and nothing completed since the previous attempt; (c) a bounded wall-clock/attempt budget per original task that scales with observed progress; (d) keep 100 retries for the batch-lock contention case (arrives via `rmm::out_of_memory` from `lock_or_prepare_batch`, not via the gate). Must produce an error that names parked bytes vs pool.
21	2. **Bookkeeping.** (a) `query_id` on every `ParkedOutput`, drop only the failing query's slots; (b) failed-query set on the engine thread that skips pending `Run`s; (c) `cancel_plan_fragment` drops the cancelled query's parked outputs and dequeues its fragments (needs a by-query removal in `LocalExchange`); (d) `drop_parked` in `run_ready_fragment`'s Err arm for pre-run translation failures; (e) a periodic sweep as a safety net. Order of landing matters: (a)+(d) are pure hygiene, (b)/(c) touch the dispatch contract.
22	3. **Cardinalities.** (a) FE-only: rows = total bytes / row width from the inferred schema in `computeFileScanNode`, using `TableFunctionTable` file sizes (no wire change; column stats stay UNKNOWN); (b) exact `num_rows` from parquet footers: new field in `PGetFileSchemaResult`, filled by the CN's `file_schema.rs` (proto + FE + CN); (c) later, per-column min/max from row-group stats; (d) no-FE alternative: CN-side translator refusal/hints, SQL join hints. Delivered as a patch in `experimental/starrocks/patches/` applied by `apply-starrocks-patches.sh`, so the FE must be rebuilt (`pixi run fe-build`). Predicted effect must be checked with `EXPLAIN COSTS` at 1 and 4 CNs: the source skeptic warns that `BROADCAST_JOIN_MEM_EXCEED_PENALTY` and zero single-node shuffle cost may still put lineitem across an exchange on 1 CN.
23	4. **Run the six on 1 CN.** (a) Same-node fragment fusion before translation: replace a receiver's `EXCHANGE_NODE` with its single local sender's node list at the `TPlan` level when every destination is this CN, so the fused plan is the standalone plan (needs `RIGHT_SEMI` in the translator for q21, finding P5); (b) spillable parked repositories: register streaming-sink outputs and receiver inputs with a registry the downgrade executor sweeps as a third tier, HOST-tier `output_row_count` and `export_packed` (five of six then fit in GPU+HOST = 279 GB; q09 marginal); (c) streaming receivers (build side first, probe streamed) is the long-term fix but touches the engine's single-flight lifecycle; (d) FE-side: real cardinalities (issue 3) may already move lineitem to the probe side of a broadcast join, which the engine can stream. The design must say which combination actually makes each of the six pass and what each costs.

1	# Fix 1 spec: fail the query fast when an OOM retry cannot make progress
2	
3	Implementation spec for an engineer working alone in the worktree
4	`/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/fix-oom-failfast` (branch off `perf/profile-sf1000` =
5	`45dab3be`, GPU 0 assigned). Source anchors below are `file:line` in that tree; the engine files this
6	fix touches are byte-identical on `origin/dev` (checked with `git diff --stat origin/dev..d24f02c4`
7	over the touched files: only `task_scheduler.{hpp,cpp}` differ, +53 lines that do not overlap the
8	edits here), so the same line numbers hold for the upstream PR. Evidence bundle:
9	`scratchpad/perf/sf1000/` (cited as `E/...`). "Measured" means read from a named file or produced by

11	
12	## 0. What was decided and why
13	
14	Two judges scored the three designs (surgical / robust / upstream). Their totals tie: surgical 43,
15	upstream 43, robust 32. Both rejected robust's config schema, constructor-signature churn and
16	exception-type change; both asked for the same set of merges. This spec is the merge:
17	
18	| piece | taken from | why |
19	|---|---|---|
20	| Decision made in the **reschedule path**, confirmed by the retry's own OOM | upstream | The gate-time abort (surgical) would fire ~40 ms earlier at best: both fire at the first retry-1 gate/OOM (section 3.6). Confirming by an actual OOM removes the pre-emptive-abort risk at negligible cost, and the reschedule path already has the error-exit shape and the operator name. |
21	| Hard lower bound `live + requested` recorded by the OOM handler | surgical | It is exact (raa accounting, section 2.3) and replaces upstream's `granted < floor` test, which judge 2 showed degenerates (the floor is raised to >= 2 x granted before the throw, so it is always true). |
22	| Pure, header-only predicate with a GPU-free Catch2 table | upstream | Reviewable decision rule; CI-testable without a GPU. |
23	| Scheduler-wide progress signals: `completed_epoch` + `inflight_first_attempts` in a small struct owned by `task_scheduler`, passed to executors through a **defaulted** extra ctor argument | robust (via judge 1) | Closes the multi-GPU blind spot (a completion on another GPU can make a subscribed GPU-0 batch convertible, `downgrade_executor.cpp:231-232`). No config, no signature break: the single test construction site keeps compiling. |
24	| `has_error()` early-out before the gate blocks | robust | Stops a failed query's queued retries from each costing the manager a blocking `make_reservation`. |
25	| `oom_reschedules` / `futile_aborts` counters in `executor_metrics` | robust | Makes component-test assertions exact. |
26	| Holder-task test that pins cucascade's IDLE semantics; arm-B log assertions; "held outside any task reservation" wording | surgical | The proof depends on partial grants being issued only when no reservation is alive; this test fails loudly if cucascade changes. |
27	| `has_disk_tier()` in the message; stale-doc fix at `execution-flow.md:150` | upstream | Gives the documented-but-uncalled hook (`downgrade_executor.hpp:155-161`) its caller. |
28	| `MAX_RETRIES = 100` and the 50 ms backoff unchanged; constant hoisted to file scope so both messages name it | all three | The #732 cross-GPU contention budget is not this fix's business. |
29	| Hysteresis = 1 (abort at the first retry whose OOM confirms the gate's verdict) | surgical / judge 2 | The bound is hard; N=2 (robust) costs a full extra round (2.4 s for q08/q09) for no safety. |
30	| Acceptance measured **from the first OOM in the engine log**, not from client start | all three | q18's first OOM is at +9.29 s because its own senders run first; q08/q09 rounds are 2.3-2.4 s. |
31	
32	Dropped: robust's YAML knob, `gpu_pipeline_executor_config`, `oom_details` on the exception, HOST-tier
33	claims (`task_scheduler.cpp:91-93` builds GPU-tier executors only); surgical's gate-time `break`;
34	upstream's per-executor `_tasks_executed` mark and creation-time snapshot (replaced by the shared
35	epoch snapshotted at the gate, which also avoids the one-round delay the single stray completion per
36	window could otherwise cause).
37	
38	## 1. Goal and non-goals
39	
40	**Goal.** A GPU pipeline task whose OOM retry provably cannot be granted what its last OOM needed fails
41	the query at that retry instead of replaying the same OOM up to 100 times, and the error names the
42	cause: bytes needed vs grantable, bytes held outside any task reservation vs the pool, bytes the
43	downgrade freed, disk-tier state, and that nothing completed or was running that could release memory.
44	
45	Measured target (1 CN, 100 GiB pool, SF1000): q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 currently die after 101.5 /
46	168.3 / 232.5 / 103.9 / 54.2 / 114.5 s (`E/cn1/runs/runs.csv`), 774.9 s of the 910.3 s sweep, with
47	17,900 reschedule warnings and 17,917 "0 bytes freed ... proceeding with partial reservation" lines.
48	After this fix each dies within one retry round of its first OOM (section 6).
49	
50	**Non-goals.**
51	- Making the six queries pass on 1 CN (fix 4), attributing the held bytes to fragments or dropping a
52	  dead query's parked output (fix 2), FE cardinalities (fix 3).
53	- Changing `MAX_RETRIES`, the backoff, the retry-floor policy (`2 x reservation`), the downgrade
54	  executor's misleading "disk not configured" WARN (`downgrade_executor.cpp:357-363`, belongs to 4b),
55	  the watchdog fingerprint, or the sink-deferral OOM path (`gpu_pipeline_task.cpp:721-751`; see
56	  decision 3).
57	- Any CN (`experimental/starrocks`), FE, proto, cucascade or configuration change. The error string
58	  already travels verbatim to the client (section 3.5).
59	
60	## 2. The measured failure and the three facts the fix rests on
61	
62	### 2.1 The loop (measured)
63	
64	`src/pipeline/gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:348` `static constexpr uint32_t MAX_RETRIES = 100;`, `:409`
65	`sleep_for(50ms)`; the only exits are the cap (`:349-364`) and `has_error()` (`:312-316`). The
66	reservation gate proceeds on a partial grant after the downgrade freed nothing (`:262-271`, the WARN
67	"after downgrade ({} bytes freed), reservation still partial ({}/{} bytes) ... proceeding with partial
68	reservation"). Per query on cn1 (`retry_stats.py`, re-run 2026-09-03):
69	
70	| query | stuck originals | reschedules | first OOM (from client start) | round 1 span | wall to die |
71	|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
72	| q05 | 25 | 2500 | +1.61 s | +1.61..+2.62 (1.01 s) | 101.5 s |
73	| q08 | 36 | 3600 | +1.73 | +1.73..+4.09 (2.36) | 168.3 |
74	| q09 | 56 | 5600 | +2.38 | +2.38..+4.68 (2.30) | 232.5 |
75	| q17 | 21 | 2100 | +1.20 | +1.20..+2.41 (1.21) | 103.9 |
76	| q18 | 23 | 2300 | +9.29 | +9.29..+9.98 (0.69) | 54.2 |
77	| q21 | 18 | 1800 | +2.68 | +2.68..+3.81 (1.13) | 114.5 |
78	
79	Every original reaches exactly retry 100; every OOM is `GPU_SCAN` index 0 with
80	`global usage 107374182400` (the limit); every one of the 17,917 gate passes freed 0 and granted
81	partially; zero reschedule lines fall outside the six windows on cn1, and none exist on the three
82	other CNs of the 4-CN sweep. The q05 chain of original task 2567 (`E/cn1/engine-cn0.log:49219-49223`,
83	`:61597`, `:61723`): first attempt granted 3,318,948,864 of 5,803,790,251 requested, OOM asking
84	748,875,880 B at peak 3,376,381,184 B; every retry granted 3,076,488,960 of the 6,637,897,728 floor,
85	freed 0, same OOM; `exceeded 100 retries` at 13:05:24.553, drain done at .624 (71 ms), CN "fragment
86	run failed" 74 ms later (`E/cn1/cluster.log`).
87	
88	Rounds are lockstep because the pool is full: the manager thread blocks in `make_reservation` until
89	the one running task releases (Quent q05 fragment 5774: `Rsv=99.940 s` of a 101.2 s window,
90	`E/cn1-quent.txt`). At most one task executes on the GPU at a time during the storm (fact A).
91	
92	### 2.2 Fact A: a partial grant means no other reservation is alive on the space
93	
94	`cucascade/src/memory/memory_space.cpp:257-266`: `make_reservation` loops on `make_reservation_or_null`
95	and only returns `make_reservation_upto(size)` when `_notification_channel->wait()` returns `IDLE`.
96	`cucascade/src/memory/notification_channel.cpp:49-60`: `IDLE` is returned only when
97	`_n_active_notifiers == 0`. Every reservation owns a notifier for its lifetime
98	(`reservation_aware_resource_adaptor.cpp:365-381`, `memory_reservation.hpp:183-198`). The upto grant is
99	`min(request, reservation_limit - total_allocated)` (`reservation_aware_resource_adaptor.cpp:375-380`
100	-> `do_reserve_upto` `:535-543` -> `add_bounded` `cucascade/include/cucascade/utils/atomics.hpp:87-97`).
101	So for a **partial** grant, `reservation_limit - granted == total_allocated at the gate == bytes held
102	outside any reservation` (parked fragment output, pinned tables, idle batches). Exact, independent of
103	`reservation_limit_fraction`; on the CN the fraction is 1.0 (`engine_settings.rs:98,102`).
104	
105	### 2.3 Fact B: a LIMIT_EXCEEDED OOM proves `live + requested > reservation`
106	
107	`reservation_aware_resource_adaptor.cpp:184-214` (`check_reservation_and_handle_overflow`): an
108	allocation charges the pool only for the part of `live + requested` that exceeds the stream's
109	reservation (`upstream_tracking_size == 0` while `post_allocation_inc < reservation_size`). The pool
110	check `_total_allocated_bytes.try_add(tracking_bytes, _capacity)` (`:465`) throws
111	`cucascade_out_of_memory(..., LIMIT_EXCEEDED, allocation_bytes, ...)` (`:477-482`). Hence a
112	LIMIT_EXCEEDED OOM implies `live + requested > reservation` strictly. `gpu_pipeline_task.cpp:433-457`
113	already computes both (`cc_oom->requested_bytes`, `_allocator->get_allocated_bytes(stream)`) and folds
114	them into the floor (`gpu_pipeline_task.hpp:99-108`); the per-stream peak is updated with the failed
115	allocation included (`:199`), which is why the logged `peak allocated 3376381184` equals
116	`live + requested` for q05 (inference from the code path; the log prints peak, not live).
117	
118	Combining A and B for a retry at gate k with a partial IDLE grant and 0 bytes freed:
119	`granted_k = limit - held_k <= limit - held_{k-1}` (held only grows during a fragment run; the CN
120	releases parked output only after the fragment finishes, `engine.rs:278-280`, finding B1) and the
121	previous OOM proved the task needs `> reservation_{k-1} >= granted_k`. The retry will OOM again, and so
122	will every later one unless something outside this task frees memory: a downgrade (shows as
123	`freed > 0`), or a task completing (shows in the shared epoch / in-flight counter).
124	
125	### 2.4 Fact C: `freed == 0` is the only trustworthy "nothing convertible" signal
126	
127	`request_downgrade(...).get()` returns the bytes freed by TIER 1 (repositories,
128	`downgrade_executor.cpp:223-232`) and TIER 2 (queued tasks, `:294-300`), `set_value(total_bytes)`
129	at `:397`. Parked sink output escapes TIER 1 by design (`streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112`, finding
130	B2). `has_viable_downgrade_target()` (`downgrade_executor.cpp:406-446`) probes HOST capacity, not
131	candidate existence, and is true in the SF1000 case (160 GiB HOST, empty). Use `freed`.
132	
133	## 3. Mechanism
134	
135	### 3.1 New header `src/include/pipeline/retry_futility.hpp` (GPU-free, header-only)
136	
137	Includes only `<atomic> <cstddef> <cstdint> <format> <optional> <string>`. No CUDA, no cucascade.
138	
139	```cpp
140	namespace sirius::pipeline {
141	
142	/// Context-wide progress signals consulted by the OOM fail-fast. One instance per task_scheduler,
143	/// shared by every gpu_pipeline_executor it owns; relaxed/acquire atomics, no locks.
144	struct execution_progress {
145	  std::atomic<std::uint64_t> completed_epoch{0};         ///< +1 per task whose execute() returned normally, any executor
146	  std::atomic<std::int64_t>  inflight_first_attempts{0}; ///< first-attempt tasks (retry_count == 0) currently inside execute(), any executor
147	};
148	
149	/// What the GPU executor's reservation gate saw for one attempt. Written by the manager thread
150	/// right before set_reservation(); read by the reschedule path after the attempt threw.
151	struct retry_gate_observation {
152	  std::size_t   requested_bytes         = 0;     ///< bytes_needs after the space-max clamp
153	  std::size_t   granted_bytes           = 0;     ///< reservation->size() handed to the task
154	  std::size_t   freed_by_downgrade      = 0;     ///< bytes the gate's downgrade request freed (0 when none ran)
155	  bool          downgrade_requested     = false; ///< the gate asked a downgrade executor (partial grant + executor present)
156	  bool          disk_tier_configured    = false; ///< downgrade_executor::has_disk_tier()
157	  std::size_t   space_max_bytes         = 0;     ///< memory_space::get_max_memory() (the reservation limit)
158	  std::uint64_t completed_epoch_at_gate = 0;     ///< execution_progress::completed_epoch read before make_reservation()
159	};
160	
161	struct retry_futility_input {
162	  bool          is_oom                      = false; ///< the exception is an oom_reschedule_exception
163	  std::uint32_t retry_count                 = 0;     ///< of the task that just threw (0 = first attempt)
164	  std::size_t   oom_required_bytes          = 0;     ///< live + requested recorded by the OOM handler; 0 = unknown
165	  std::optional<retry_gate_observation> gate;        ///< this attempt's gate observation
166	  std::uint64_t completed_epoch_now         = 0;
167	  std::int64_t  inflight_first_attempts_now = 0;
168	};
169	
170	/// Returns std::nullopt when another retry may succeed; otherwise the human-readable reason it
171	/// cannot (used verbatim in the query error). Pure: no I/O, no globals.
172	inline std::optional<std::string> assess_retry_futility(const retry_futility_input& in);
173	
174	}  // namespace sirius::pipeline
175	```
176	
177	Decision rule, in this order (each early-return is one row of the test table in 4.1):
178	
179	1. `!in.is_oom` -> nullopt (CUDA-launch reschedules keep the plain 100-retry budget).
180	2. `in.retry_count == 0` -> nullopt (a first attempt never fails fast; partial first attempts often succeed).
181	3. `!in.gate` -> nullopt (defensive: the gate did not record).
182	4. `gate.granted_bytes >= gate.requested_bytes` -> nullopt (full grant: the gate was not the constraint; this is
183	   the #732 contention shape and the existing `xl_task` test).
184	5. `gate.freed_by_downgrade != 0` -> nullopt (spilling is making progress; fix 4b lives here).
185	6. `in.oom_required_bytes == 0 || in.oom_required_bytes <= gate.granted_bytes` -> nullopt (unknown need, or it would fit).

110	## 3. Design in one paragraph
111	
112	*The engine holds parked state; the CN decides when a query is over.* Parked output is keyed by the
113	query id every run already carries (`FragmentLabel.query_id`, `fragment_executor.rs:57-63`, filled by
114	`fragment_label` at `compute_node_service.rs:1584-1589`). A query is declared over by exactly three
115	events, all terminal on the FE side: the engine's own `Err` for a run of that query (marked on the engine
116	thread before its next dequeue), a CN-side failure of a fragment of that query (`fail_fragment`), or an
117	FE `cancel_plan_fragment` carrying that query id. Each event retires the query: drops its parked
118	fragments, poisons its slots with the cause, marks it in a shared `RetiredQueries` set, and (from the
119	CN) purges its rendezvous state and releases its staged leases. Four gates consult the marks: the engine
120	refuses a `Run` of a retired query as the first statement inside `run_fragment_inner` (so the lease
121	sweep at `engine.rs:462-478` still runs); the engine refuses to *park* output of a query retired while
122	the fragment ran; the dispatch worker skips a queued fragment of a failed query before translating it
123	(releasing its staged batches, emitting no `fragment run started`); `process_fragment` refuses a late
124	arrival of a failed query before translation. No knobs, no timer, no wire change.

637	### 5.2 Default dispatch mode (async off, not the campaign setting; tested in CI, smoke-tested at SF1000)
638	
639	Senders run inside their RPC threads and queue in the engine channel behind the failing `Run`. The
640	engine marks the query at its own `Err` before responding, so every queued `Run` of it is refused at gate
641	1 with its leases swept, and logs `fragment run started` / `fragment run failed ... already retired`
642	with `elapsed_ms` of a channel round trip. A sender arriving after the failure is refused at gate 4 before
643	translation (RPC `INTERNAL_ERROR`, which the FE ignores: it is already cancelling,
644	`DefaultCoordinator.java:1054-1057`). Commit 2's inline recording makes `failure_of` true on this node
645	for an inline failure too.

650	one small mutex lock per run at gate 1 and one at gate 2 (microseconds against fragment runs of 4 ms to

652	`cancels=N`) each cost one non-blocking channel send, one `RetiredQueries::mark`, one empty
653	`retire_receiver` and one empty engine `retire` (DEBUG line). `results.cancel` is unchanged, so delivered
654	rows are never clobbered (`cancel_fails_only_a_waiting_entry`, `result_store.rs:490-510`). No plan, memory
655	or ordering change; warm medians should be within run-to-run noise (6%).

665	makes it a success (it is a microsecond window against an FE round trip, and impossible in inline mode,

2

4	`/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/fix-files-cardinality` (branch off `perf/profile-sf1000` = `45dab3be`;
5	the StarRocks submodule there already has the two existing patches applied: `git -C experimental/starrocks/starrocks
6	status` shows `Config.java`, `FileScanNode.java`, `internal_service.proto` modified). Every `file:line` below was

8	`FET` = `experimental/starrocks/starrocks/fe/fe-core/src/test/java/com/starrocks`, `CN` = `experimental/starrocks/src`,

14	
15	## 0. Decision record
16	
17	Both judges scored the three designs (surgical 19/23, upstream 19/21, robust 14/14). Judge 1 chose upstream, judge 2
18	chose surgical "in the upstream design's shape". Those are the same thing: PR-A of upstream *is* the surgical design
19	with the estimate living on `TableFunctionTable` instead of inside `StatisticsCalculator`. This spec implements:
20	
21	- **PR-A** (FE patch, no wire change): bytes / row width estimate (the Hive no-statistics rule), one mutable Config
22	  knob, FE unit tests, harness and docs. Deliverable of issue 3 on its own; identical to the surgical design.
23	- **PR-B** (stacked on PR-A): one `optional int64 num_rows = 3` on `PGetFileSchemaResult`, filled by the CN from the
24	  parquet footers it already opens, consumed by the FE as the preferred source. Makes the leaf counts exact and the
25	  EXPLAIN goldens independent of the dataset copy. ~40 lines of Rust, +3 proto lines, one CI step change.
26	
27	Merged in from the other designs as the judges asked: explicit `isListFilesOnly()` guard; `getFileColumns()` that
28	excludes `columns_from_path`; `tableRowCountMayInaccurate=true` only on the fallback path; one FE INFO line per
29	statement and CN span fields; a `PlanTestBase` test with injected statistics asserting join side and distribution;
30	the `build.rs` guard extended for the new proto token; `.github/workflows/experimental.yml` switched to
31	`apply-starrocks-patches.sh`; `SET GLOBAL cbo_cte_reuse = false` in the bench bring-up with read-back; the mutable-knob
32	A/B procedure on one FE; goldens worded as **post-predicate** FileScanNode cardinalities; string equality on an
33	UNKNOWN column is **1.0** (not 0.5), `colA < colB` is **0.5**.
34	
35	**Not** in this spec (decided at the EXPLAIN gate, see section 11): the robust design's Part B cost levers
36	(`exec_mem_limit`, `enable_local_shuffle_agg=false`, `broadcast_row_limit`, a probe-penalty cap in
37	`HashJoinCostModel`) = the plan's fix 4(d), and per-file / per-column footer statistics (proto surface without a
38	measured payoff: no decision examined changes sign between the 0.25 default and the footer range).
39	
40	## 1. Goal and non-goals
41	
42	**Goal.** Every FILES() scan the FE plans carries its real row count (exact from parquet footers when the CN
43	reports it, else bytes / typed row width), so join sides, BROADCAST/SHUFFLE choice, the broadcast guard, semi/anti
44	commutation and CTE costing stop being arithmetic on column widths. Observable: `EXPLAIN COSTS` prints
45	`cardinality: 5999989709` on the lineitem `FileScanNode` instead of `cardinality: 1`; `card_all_one=False` for all
46	22 TPC-H plans.
47	
48	**Non-goals (stated so nobody scores this fix against them).**
49	
50	1. It does not make q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 pass on 1 CN. Inference from the FE cost code, agreed by all three
51	   designs and both judges (section 8.1): with real counts and stock settings the FE still hash-partitions
52	   lineitem at 1 CN whenever the other side is above ~5M estimated rows. Fix 4 (fusion or spill) is what makes the
53	   six pass; fix 1 makes the still-wrong plans die in seconds.
54	2. No column statistics (min/max/NDV). Every column stays `ColumnStatistic.unknown()`.
55	3. No engine (`src/`) change, no translator change, no change to scan split assignment (`FileScanNode.java:545-549`
56	   is bytes-based and untouched), no change to the receiver-first exchange mechanism (B1).
57	4. No cost-model change. Session-variable experiments belong to the gate, not to this patch.

The physical FILES() operator falls through to `visitOperator` (`FE/sql/optimizer/operator/OperatorVisitor.java:454-456`) and is never re-derived on the main path (`PlanFragmentBuilder.java:4294` uses `optExpression.getStatistics()`), so the logical override is what decides today |

85	### 3.1 PR-A, FE: `TableFunctionTable` owns the estimate
86	
87	`FE/catalog/TableFunctionTable.java`. Add after the `fileStatuses` field (`:188`):
88	
89	```java
90	// Row total the compute node read from the parquet footers with the schema (PGetFileSchemaResult.num_rows);
91	// -1 when it reported none. Set only by getFileSchema(); PR-A never sets it.
92	private long footerRowCount = -1;
93	```
94	
95	Add public accessors (place after `loadFileList()` `:300-302`):
96	
97	```java
98	/** Bytes of the listed files (directories excluded); the numerator of the row estimate. */
99	public long getTotalFileBytes() {
100	    long bytes = 0;
101	    for (TBrokerFileStatus f : fileStatuses) {
102	        if (!f.isDir) {
103	            bytes += Math.max(0L, f.size);
104	        }
105	    }
106	    return bytes;
107	}
108	
109	/** The inferred file schema without the trailing columns_from_path entries, which occupy no file bytes. */
110	public List<Column> getFileColumns() {
111	    List<Column> all = getFullSchema();
112	    int fileColumns = all.size() - columnsFromPath.size();
113	    return all.subList(0, Math.max(0, fileColumns));
114	}
115	
116	/** True when estimateRowCount() returns a footer total rather than the bytes / width estimate. */
117	public boolean hasExactRowCount() {
118	    return footerRowCount > 0;
119	}
120	
121	/**
122	 * Row count for the CBO. The footer total the compute node returned with the schema when present, else
123	 * HiveStatisticsProvider.getEstimatedRowCount's rule (total bytes / sum of type widths), else 1. Each width is
124	 * floored at 1 so a zero-width type cannot zero the denominator (the one deviation from the Hive rule).
125	 */
126	public long estimateRowCount() {
127	    if (!Config.files_scan_estimate_row_count || listFilesOnly || fileStatuses.isEmpty()) {
128	        return 1;
129	    }
130	    if (footerRowCount > 0) {
131	        return footerRowCount;
132	    }
133	    long bytes = getTotalFileBytes();
134	    long width = 0;
135	    for (Column c : getFileColumns()) {
136	        width += Math.max(1, c.getType().getTypeSize());
137	    }
138	    if (bytes <= 0 || width <= 0) {
139	        return 1;
140	    }
141	    return Math.max(1L, bytes / width);
142	}
143	```

146	one-row-per-entry schema (`setSchemaForListFiles` `:278-280`) and must keep 1. UNLOAD tables
147	(`TableFunctionTable(List<Column>, Map, SessionVariable)` `:245`) never populate `fileStatuses` and return 1.

162	
163	```java
164	@Override
165	public Void visitLogicalTableFunctionTableScan(LogicalTableFunctionTableScanOperator node, ExpressionContext context) {
166	    return computeFileScanNode(node, context, node.getTable(), node.getColRefToColumnMetaMap());
167	}
168	
169	// New. Mirrors the visitLogicalFileScan / visitPhysicalFileScan pair at :655-662; today the physical FILES()
170	// operator falls through to OperatorVisitor.visitOperator (:454-456). Defensive: nothing re-derives it on the
171	// main path, but a future physical re-derivation must not silently return to 1 row.
172	@Override
173	public Void visitPhysicalTableFunctionTableScan(PhysicalTableFunctionTableScanOperator node, ExpressionContext context) {
174	    return computeFileScanNode(node, context, node.getTable(), node.getColRefToColumnMetaMap());
175	}
176	
177	@Override
178	public Void visitLogicalFileScan(LogicalFileScanOperator node, ExpressionContext context) {
179	    return computeFileScanNode(node, context, node.getTable(), node.getColRefToColumnMetaMap());
180	}
181	
182	@Override
183	public Void visitPhysicalFileScan(PhysicalFileScanOperator node, ExpressionContext context) {
184	    return computeFileScanNode(node, context, node.getTable(), node.getColRefToColumnMetaMap());
185	}
186	
187	private Void computeFileScanNode(Operator node, ExpressionContext context, Table table,
188	                                 Map<ColumnRefOperator, Column> columnRefOperatorColumnMap) {
189	    Statistics.Builder builder = Statistics.builder();
190	    for (ColumnRefOperator columnRefOperator : columnRefOperatorColumnMap.keySet()) {
191	        builder.addColumnStatistic(columnRefOperator, ColumnStatistic.unknown());
192	    }
193	    // Column statistics stay unknown (no footer min/max/NDV). A FILES() scan gets the row total the compute node
194	    // read from the parquet footers, else total bytes / row width, else 1. The external FILE table keeps 1.
195	    long rows = 1;
196	    boolean exact = false;
197	    if (table instanceof TableFunctionTable) {
198	        TableFunctionTable files = (TableFunctionTable) table;
199	        rows = files.estimateRowCount();
200	        exact = files.hasExactRowCount();
201	    }
202	    builder.setOutputRowCount(rows);
203	    // Honest only on the bytes / width path. Consumers of the flag (DeriveStatsTask:72-77 MV only, DataSkew:161/194,
204	    // StatisticsEstimateUtils:117, CostModel:371) are already short-circuited by the unknown column statistics.
205	    builder.setTableRowCountMayInaccurate(rows != 1 && !exact);
206	    context.setStatistics(builder.build());
207	    return visitOperator(node, context);
208	}

17	## 1. Goal and non-goals
18	
19	### Goal
20	
21	On one CN, when a data-stream sender fragment's **only** destination is a receiver **on this CN**
22	whose `EXCHANGE_NODE` expects **exactly one** sender, do not run the sender. Park its *plan* in the
23	rendezvous instead of its *rows*; when the receiver becomes ready, splice the sender's `TPlan.nodes`
24	in place of the receiver's `EXCHANGE_NODE`, merge the exec params the translator reads, and run the
25	fused fragment as one plan. The engine's DuckDB optimizer, which already runs on every fragment
26	(`src/sirius_ffi.cpp:134-138`, with `JOIN_ORDER` and `BUILD_SIDE_PROBE_SIDE` enabled: the disabled set
27	at `:233-243` is `IN_CLAUSE, COMPRESSED_MATERIALIZATION, STATISTICS_PROPAGATION, COLUMN_LIFETIME,
28	LATE_MATERIALIZATION`), then sees the lineitem scan as an ordinary `ReadRel` inside the join fragment
29	and puts it on the probe side, so lineitem streams through the join instead of being parked whole.
30	
31	Measured target (perf/cn1-cnlog.txt, perf/cn1/dump): q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 die on 1 CN at SF1000
32	with a 100 GiB pool after 54-232 s of OOM reschedules (775 s of a 910 s sweep); each is a bare
33	lineitem `FILE_SCAN_NODE` alone in a fragment whose `DATA_STREAM_SINK` is `HASH_PARTITIONED` with one
34	local destination (`fragment-0141.txt` node 8 -> exchange 9; `0208` 3 -> 4; `0220` 3 -> 4; `0427`
35	0 -> 1; `0437` 9 -> 10; `0504` 12 -> 13). Standalone Sirius on the same GPU and pool runs all six in
36	2.7-6.5 s warm and matches the oracle exactly (perf/compare-standalone-failed.txt, perf/results-failed.md).

38	### Shipped in this PR (PR 1)
39	
40	- Fusion of **leaf** senders (no `EXCHANGE_NODE` of their own) with a `HASH_PARTITIONED`
41	  single-destination local sink into a plain exchange whose parent is not an aggregation. Knob
42	  `SIRIUS_CN_FRAGMENT_FUSION = off | leaf | leaf-any`, default `leaf`.
43	- Complete fallback: every decline is today's run-and-park path. No decision is taken after a
44	  sender has been deferred that could fail the query for a shape that passes today.
45	- Predicted effect (inference, sections 8-9): q05 q08 q17 q18 pass (high confidence), q09 passes
46	  with little headroom (medium), **q21 most likely still OOMs** (medium; the leaf rule keeps the

98	## 3. Design decisions (with the judges' reasoning)
99	
100	1. **Leaf, HASH_PARTITIONED, non-aggregation parent is the shipped default.** It is a strict subset
101	   of the upstream behaviour, keeps 11 of the 15 passing 1-CN plans byte-identical, keeps exact
102	   stream cardinalities at every non-leaf boundary (the BJ-4 hazard, perf report C2, is bounded to
103	   leaves whose relative sizes are >= 5x apart), and needs no remote-path change.
104	2. **All fusability checks run at defer time with both sender and receiver params in hand.** A
105	   refusal is a logged decline to today's path, never a query failure. This fixes the one
106	   as-written flaw the judges found in the upstream design (sender-side refusals evaluated at
107	   fold time after the sender had been deferred).
108	3. **Pure splice lives in the translator crate** (`fusion.rs`, `FusionRefusal` enum), because that
109	   crate already owns `TPlan -> Substrait` and its invariants, and it is testable without an
110	   engine. The CN owns policy (mode), routing and the rendezvous.
111	4. **`SenderSource::LocalPlan { params, inputs }`** carries the deferred sender's own exchange
112	   inputs so PR 2 (middle fragments) is a fold extension, not an alias map. In PR 1 `inputs` is
113	   always empty.
114	5. **Three-valued knob through `tunable.rs`** (rejected on a bad value, logged at bring-up):
115	   `off | leaf | leaf-any`. `leaf-any` (all single-destination local leaves, any partition type) is
116	   the experiment arm for q09's ~31 GB of broadcast parking; it is not the default.
117	6. **No `RIGHT_SEMI` translator arm is needed here**: the flip happens inside the engine after
118	   fusion, as it already does today for q04 (section 2, last rows).
119	7. **Conservative aggregation rule**: decline when the exchange's parent is *any*
120	   `AGGREGATION_NODE`, not only `AggPhase::Merge`. No TPC-H exchange has a non-merge aggregation
121	   parent (`perf/survey/plan-summary.txt`), so the broader rule buys nothing and the narrower one
122	   is easier to reason about. Also decline when the **sender root** is a `Partial` aggregation
123	   (`agg_phase::classify`, `agg_phase.rs:44-80`): partial states must cross a real boundary, and
124	   the "partial avg must be the fragment root" invariant (`node_translator.rs:404-414`) would
125	   otherwise be violated by the splice.
126

366	```rust
367	impl ServiceCore {
368	    /// Tries to defer a sender into its local receiver instead of running it. Returns the
369	    /// receivers this completed (to dispatch) or `None` when the sender must take today's path.
370	    /// Every check runs here, before anything is deferred; a decline is logged and never an error.
371	    fn try_defer_sender(
372	        &self,
373	        params: &TExecPlanFragmentParams,          // descriptor-resolved
374	    ) -> std::result::Result<Option<Vec<ReadyFragment>>, String> {
375	        let mode = self.fragment_fusion();                     // AtomicU8 -> FusionMode
376	        if mode == FusionMode::Off { return Ok(None); }        // debug!("fragment fusion skipped", reason="off")
377	        let shape = match fusion::sender_shape(params) {
378	            Ok(shape) => shape,
379	            Err(refusal) => { debug!(..reason = %refusal, "fragment fusion skipped"); return Ok(None); }
380	        };
381	        // Policy (PR 1: leaves only)
382	        if !shape.is_leaf { debug!(..reason = "sender has exchange inputs", ..); return Ok(None); }
383	        if mode == FusionMode::Leaf && shape.partition != TPartitionType::HASH_PARTITIONED {
384	            debug!(..reason = "leaf mode fuses HASH_PARTITIONED sinks only", ..); return Ok(None);
385	        }
386	        if !matches!(self.route_destination(shape.destination)?, DestinationRoute::Local) {
387	            debug!(..reason = "remote destination", ..); return Ok(None);
388	        }
389	        let key = ExchangeKey {
390	            fragment_instance_id: FragmentInstanceId::from(&shape.destination.fragment_instance_id),
391	            node_id: shape.dest_node_id,
392	        };
393	        let plan = LocalPlan { params: params.clone(), inputs: Vec::new() };
394	        match self.exchanges.offer_local_plan(key, shape.sender_id, plan,
395	                |receiver| fusion::fusable_edge(receiver, key.node_id, params))? {
396	            FuseOffer::Fused(ready) => {
397	                info!(%query_id, %sender_fragment_instance_id, %receiver_fragment_instance_id,
398	                      exchange = key.node_id, mode = ?mode, "fused sender fragment into its local receiver");
399	                Ok(Some(ready.into_iter().collect()))
400	            }
401	            FuseOffer::Declined { skip, .. } => {
402	                info!(%query_id, %sender_fragment_instance_id, %receiver_fragment_instance_id,
403	                      exchange = key.node_id, reason = %skip, "fragment fusion skipped");
404	                Ok(None)
405	            }
406	        }
407	    }
408	}

412	multi-destination, not a data-stream sink) are `debug!` because every broadcast leaf hits one on

414	`ReceiverExpectsMany`, `ExchangeAlreadySourced`, `Structural`) are `info!` because they are the
415	arrival-order and plan-shape regressions the acceptance arm counts (section 8: `fragment fusion
416	skipped` must be 0 for the six).

444	let (params, inputs, fused_senders) = Self::fold_deferred_plans(ready)?;

449	// then exactly today's code over `inputs` and `&params`; `dump_fragment(&params)` at :1358 now
450	// dumps the FUSED params, which pairs with the plan-NNNN.substrait the engine runs.
451	
452	/// Splices every deferred sender plan into the receiver's params. Returns the fused params, the
453	/// remaining (streamed) inputs, and the absorbed sender instance ids. A refusal here is a bug:
454	/// the same checks passed at defer time on the same two params.
455	fn fold_deferred_plans(ready: ReadyFragment)
456	    -> std::result::Result<(TExecPlanFragmentParams, Vec<ReadyExchangeInput>, Vec<FragmentInstanceId>), String>
457	{
458	    let mut params = ready.params;
459	    let mut streamed = Vec::new();
460	    let mut fused = Vec::new();
461	    let mut worklist = ready.inputs;                       // PR 2: a deferred plan's own inputs join this list
462	    while let Some(input) = worklist.pop() {
463	        match input.sources.as_slice() {
464	            [SenderSource::LocalPlan(_)] => {
465	                let SenderSource::LocalPlan(plan) = input.sources.into_iter().next().unwrap() else { unreachable!() };
466	                let sender_id = Self::fragment_instance_id(&plan.params);
467	                params = fusion::splice(params, input.node_id, &plan.params).map_err(|refusal| format!(
468	                    "fragment fusion: splicing deferred sender {sender} into receiver {receiver} at exchange {} \
469	                     failed after passing the defer-time checks: {refusal}", input.node_id, ..))?;
470	                fused.extend(sender_id);
471	                worklist.extend(plan.inputs);              // empty in PR 1
472	            }
473	            sources if sources.iter().any(|s| matches!(s, SenderSource::LocalPlan(_))) => {
474	                return Err(format!("exchange node {} mixes a deferred sender plan with {} other sender source(s)",
475	                                   input.node_id, sources.len() - 1));
476	            }
477	            _ => streamed.push(input),
478	        }
479	    }
480	    streamed.sort_by_key(|input| input.node_id);           // keep take_ready's deterministic order
481	    Ok((params, streamed, fused))
482	}
483	```

769	Cost = `0.5 cpu + 2 mem + 1.5 net` (`CostModel.java:129-135`). BROADCAST exchange: `mem = S_B`, `net = S_B`,
770	x1000 when `S_B > exec_mem_limit` 2 GiB (`:419-429`; `aliveBackendNumber = 0` here because Sirius CNs register as
771	COMPUTE NODEs). SHUFFLE exchange: `cpu = S`, `net = S` or 0 on a single registered node with
772	`enable_local_shuffle_agg` (`:432-441`). Hash join (`HashJoinCostModel.java:86-156`): broadcast probe penalty
773	`clamp(ln(R_rows / 1e5), 1, 12)`, shuffle penalty `clamp(ln(R_rows / 1e5) - log2(2 pf), 1, 3)`. For q05's
774	lineitem join (L = 6e9 x 28 B, R = orders x customer ~3.75e8 x 12 B): BROADCAST ~718 even with the x1000 penalty
775	removed vs SHUFFLE ~350 (both judges re-derived this). Broadcast wins at 1 CN only for builds under ~5M rows
776	(nation, region, supplier, filtered part). Every one of the six joins lineitem to an orders- or partsupp-derived
777	side of 1e8-1e9 rows, so all six keep the P1 shape. The robust design's Part B (raise `exec_mem_limit`, count
778	single-node shuffle bytes, cap the broadcast probe penalty at 3) flips the sign; that is fix 4(d), gate-decided.

773	## 9. Risks and how the reviewer should probe them
774	
775	1. **Estimated instead of exact cardinality for fused leaves (medium).** Today a receiver plans
776	   with exact parked row counts (`engine.rs:551-587`); after fusion a leaf carries the parquet
777	   footer count x 0.2. A wrong pick costs memory/time (OOM bounded by fix 1), never a wrong answer,
778	   because a single-destination sink is the identity on rows and every exchange decoration that
779	   could change results is refused (`sort_info`, `limit`, `offset`, `conjuncts`, aggregation
780	   parent). Probe: arm B's build-side check on q02/q07/q13/q20; arm C's A/B.
781	2. **q21 flips onto l3 (medium, expected).** Fused F07 is `LEFT SEMI(build l2 scan) over RIGHT
782	   ANTI(left = l3 scan, right = stream 9)` (`fragment-0500.txt` node 10 children in preorder:
783	   exchange 2 then exchange 9). The translator lowers `RIGHT_ANTI` to `Right` + `IS NULL`
784	   (`node_translator.rs:1750, 1837-1844`), and `TryFlipJoinChildren` compares stream 9 (exact
785	   ~1.85e9 rows) with the l3 estimate (6.0e9 x 0.2 = 1.2e9): the exact side looks bigger, DuckDB
786	   builds on l3 (actual 3.8e9 rows, the 77.76 GB measured in `cn1-quent.txt`) and OOMs. Probe: read
787	   the fused F07's `HASH_JOIN (id=10)` build port in engine-cn0.log before looking at the time.
788	   Route to a pass: PR 2 (`all`) makes stream 9 a join estimate too; fix 3 (real FE cardinalities)
789	   may reorder the supplier join below the anti as standalone does.
790	3. **Translator invariants on the spliced plan (low).** `merge_exchange_overrides` is protected by
791	   `AggregationParent` (a leaf can never contain a `Merge` aggregation: it has no exchange to read
792	   from) and `PartialAggregationRoot`; `common_slots_consumed_above` and
793	   `refuse_carried_join_child` by `CommonSlotProjection` (verified no TPC-H exposure: the 10
794	   fragments with `common_slot_map: Some` in `perf/cn1/dump` are q01's F02 x3 and six q14/q08
795	   fragments, all sinking into merge-fed or broadcast exchanges that are declined anyway);
796	   `ensure_consumed` by `MalformedSenderPlan`. Probe: the translator tests in 5.1/5.2 and the
797	   `fused_receiver_dump_is_the_fused_plan` test; read one fused `fragment-NNNN.txt` from arm A.
798	4. **Arrival order (low).** Fusion needs the receiver registered before the leaf arrives. The FE
799	   deploys stage by stage from the root (`Deployer.java:208-215`) and this is measured for q05
800	   (`cluster.log:4142-4202`); under `enable_single_node_schedule` (default false,
801	   `SessionVariable.java:3337`) RPCs could race and the design declines, logging
802	   `NoPendingReceiver`. Probe: arm A's `fragment fusion skipped = 0`.
803	5. **Blast radius (low).** 11 of 15 passing 1-CN plans are byte-identical; 4 CNs untouched by
804	   construction (arm D). The only shared code touched on the remote path is the `SenderSource`
805	   enum gaining a variant; `push_remote_frame`'s `let SenderSource::Remote {..} = source else`
806	   (`local_exchange.rs:201-212`) already errors on a non-remote collision, so a `LocalPlan` under a
807	   remote frame's key is a loud error, not a silent misread.
808	6. **Host state after cancel (low).** A deferred plan is thrift (hundreds of KB), no GPU memory.
809	   `forget_query` (4.6) drops it on cancel; without it (if fix 2 owns removal) it lives as long as
810	   a parked slot does today. Probe: `cancel_drops_deferred_plans` test.
811	7. **Telemetry and tooling (low).** A fused sender has no `fragment run started` line and no
812	   Quent query of its own; `cnlog_extract.py`'s `frags=` shrinks; arrival-time dumps are unchanged
813	   but the receiver's ready-time dump is the fused plan. The `fused sender fragment` line carries
814	   the sender's instance id so a stitch stays possible.
815	8. **Huge `Debug` output (low, easy to miss).** `TExecPlanFragmentParams`'s derived `Debug` is
816	   the 23k-line dump. `LocalPlan` must implement `Debug` by hand and no error string may embed
817	   params. Probe: grep the diff for `{:?}` / `?plan` on anything holding params.
818	9. **Sink identity assumptions (low).** `sender_shape` refuses `limit`, non-empty
819	   `output_columns` and `output_exprs`, the same three shapes `execute_fragment_with_inputs`
820	   (`:1079-1094`) and `translate_fragment_with_exchange_inputs` (`lib.rs:291-312`) treat
821	   specially today, so no sink-side transformation is ever dropped by the splice.

228	**Mechanism, corrected by the source skeptic.** The cited term `CostModel.visitPhysicalDistribution` BROADCAST = `outputSize * aliveBackendNumber` (`CostModel.java:419-424`) is inert in this deployment: the Sirius CNs register as COMPUTE NODEs (`experimental/starrocks/src/lib.rs:210-212` `ALTER SYSTEM ADD COMPUTE NODE`; cn4/cluster.log:201 `run_mode is shared_data`), and `ctx.getAliveBackendNumber()` counts only BACKENDs (`system/SystemInfoService.java:1047`), so it is 0. With every child at 1 row, `Statistics.getOutputSize` is the sum of projected type widths, and the rule reduces to: broadcast the right side iff its row width is below roughly the left width at 1 CN, and below roughly a quarter of it at 4 CNs. This reproduces every observed decision (q03: build 16 B vs probe 24 B -> BROADCAST at 1 CN, PARTITIONED at 4; customer 4 B vs orders 20 B -> BROADCAST at both; the survivors q22 `o_custkey` 4 B, q07 `c_custkey+c_nationkey`, q02 `ps_partkey+min` are the narrow ones). `checkBroadcastRowCountLimit` (`task/EnforceAndCostTask.java:281-325`) never fires because it needs `rightChildStats.getOutputRowCount() > 15,000,000` (`SessionVariable.java:1833`).

Result: q12 and q19 flip to BROADCAST (saving ~26 GB), q03 and q10's customer join stay PARTITIONED, q14 stays a wash. Getting the q03/q10 plans additionally requires raising `broadcast_row_limit` / `broadcast_right_table_scale_factor` (`SessionVariable.java:1833-1836`), or column statistics (NDV) for FILES(), or neutralising the probe-cache penalty in `HashJoinCostModel` (`BROADCAST_MAT_RATIO` 12 vs `SHUFFLE_MAX_RATIO` 3).

ON` syntax, not the kit's comma joins, and a hint disables reorder/commutativity for that join. `broadcast_row_limit = 0` forces shuffle everywhere (`EnforceAndCostTask.java:312-314`), which would help q22/q07/q02 and hurt q03/q12/q19. `cbo_debug_alive_backend_number` (`SessionVariable.java:1823`) changes only the BE count and cannot reproduce the 1-CN plan at 4 CNs.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Quent-instrumented CN capture at SF1000. usage: capture-cn.sh <num_cns> <tag> <timeout_s> <runs_after_warmup> q01 q03 ...
# Cluster: 100GiB GPU pool, 16GiB staging, 160GiB host per CN (the perf plan's retime configuration), watchdog 300 s,

N=$1; TAG=$2; TO=$3; RUNS=$4; shift 4
OUT=$SP/perf/sf1000/$TAG; mkdir -p $OUT/quent

[ "$N" = 1 ] && { export SIRIUS_CN_DUMP_FRAGMENTS=$OUT/dump; mkdir -p $OUT/dump; rm -f $OUT/dump/*; }

echo "alive=$n after $((i*3))s"; nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,memory.used --format=csv,noheader | tr '\n' ' '; echo

echo "##### CAPTURE $TAG DONE $(date -u +%T)"

# Integration of the four SF1000 fix specs: order, conflicts, combined verification

Written 2026-09-03 after reading `oom-failfast-SPEC.md`, `parked-bookkeeping-SPEC.md`,
`files-cardinality-SPEC.md`, `fragment-fusion-SPEC.md`, the plan
(`~/.claude/plans/sf1000-top4-fixes-plan.md`) and the report sections 3B/3C/4. Every `file:line` was
re-read in `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf` at `45dab3be`; all four `fix-*` worktrees are at
the same commit and clean (`git log -1`, `git status` on each). "Measured" = copied from a named file
under `scratchpad/perf/sf1000/` (`E/`); everything else is inference and says so. Section 7 lists the
edits made to the four spec files.

## 0. Verdict in five lines

1. The four specs are compatible. Two contradictions and one wrong prediction had to be fixed in the
   specs (section 2.7); none requires a redesign.
2. Land in the order **fix 1 -> fix 2 -> fix 4a -> (item 5) -> fix 3**. Fix 1 has no shared files; fix 2
   establishes the by-query removal that fusion must reuse; fix 3 is last because its FE rebuild takes
   hours, its `EXPLAIN` gate must precede any 1-CN sweep, and its plan changes invalidate fusion's golden
   counts (so fusion is measured against today's plans first).
3. Only fix 4a changes the pass/fail set at 1 CN (q05 q08 q17 q18 pass, q09 probably, q21 probably not).
   Fixes 1-3 change time-to-fail, hygiene and plan shape. No two fixes fight on the six.
4. Two source files are edited by two specs each (`compute_node_service.rs`: fixes 2, 3B, 4a;
   `local_exchange.rs`: fixes 2, 4a) plus two docs (`TUNABLES.md`: 3, 4; `DEMO.md`: 2, 3, 4). All are
   resolvable by ordering; the one semantic overlap (`cancel_plan_fragment`) is resolved in favour of fix 2.
5. The combined verification is six arms, ~2 h of box time excluding the FE build, in the order of
   section 6. The final integration sweep is the first time the six are ever run at 4 CNs.

## 1. Which fix rescues which of the six (1 CN, 100 GiB pool)

| query | today (measured, `E/cn1/runs/runs.csv`) | fix 1 | fix 2 | fix 3 (knob on) | fix 4a `leaf` | all four |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| q05 | OOM at 101.5 s | fails at ~2.9 s | no change (leak 0 GB before it) | still hash-partitions lineitem (inference, fix 3 App. B) | **pass** (high) | pass |
| q08 | OOM 168.3 s | ~4.3 s | leftovers of q05 (4.7 GB) gone | same | **pass** (high) | pass |
| q09 | OOM 232.5 s | ~4.9 s | q08 leftovers (8.8 GB) gone | same | **pass** (medium; ~31 GB of broadcasts still parked) | pass (medium); `leaf-any` is the fallback |
| q17 | OOM 103.9 s | ~2.6 s | q09+q16 leftovers (38.2 GB) gone | same | **pass** (high) | pass |
| q18 | OOM 54.2 s | ~10.2 s (own senders first) | no leftovers today | same | **pass** (high) | pass |
| q21 | OOM 114.5 s | ~4.0 s | q17 leftover (4.0 GB) gone | same | **likely still OOM**: fused F07 builds on l3 (inference, fusion spec 9.2) | fails, but see 2.2: not necessarily fast |

Sources: fix 1 table 3.6; fix 2 section 5.1 and report B4 ("no pass/fail was decided by the leak");
fix 3 non-goal 1 and Appendix B; fusion section 1 and 7. Fix 3 at 4 CNs: the six were never run at 4 CNs
(report 5.1); the expected outcome is pass regardless of fix 3 (per-CN lineitem share 31-61 GB, inference).

**Do two fixes fight on the six?** No.

- Fix 1 and fix 4a divide labour by fix 1's rule 5 (`freed_by_downgrade != 0 -> keep retrying`): a fused
  fragment holds its join build in inter-pipeline repositories that the downgrade sweep can spill
  (`src/pipeline/repository_wiring_materializer.cpp:68-69` registers each wiring port with the per-query
  manager; TIER 1 iterates those managers, `src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp:223-232`), so the
  fail-fast stays quiet while spilling makes progress and only fires when nothing is convertible. That is
  the intended division, but it also means the fusion spec's "with fix 1 in the same build q21 dies in
  seconds" was wrong (2.2).
- Fix 3 and fix 4a are complementary at 1 CN: fix 3 is predicted (inference, fix 3 risk 8.1) to flip q03
  and q12 from BROADCAST to PARTITIONED, which would park ~78 GB / ~36 GB of lineitem / orders; that
  shape (bare leaf, `HASH_PARTITIONED`, one local destination) is exactly what `leaf` fuses, so with both
  in the build those two keep streaming. Fix 3 alone at 1 CN with the knob on is a regression risk for q03.
- Fix 2 and fix 4a overlap in code, not in effect: a deferred plan parks nothing, so fusion shrinks fix 2's
  exposure at 1 CN; fix 2's cancel path must remove deferred plans, which its per-instance
  `retire_receiver` already does (2.3).

## 2. Interactions checked

### 2.1 Fix 1 (fail fast) vs fix 2 (Err-path bookkeeping): compatible

- **Same Err path, earlier and with a new text.** Fix 1 exits through `completion_handler::report_error`
  exactly like the `MAX_RETRIES` path (fix 1 spec 3.4 "same exit shape"), so the chain
  `sirius_engine.cpp` rethrow -> `streaming_fragment::run` -> `ffi::Fragment::run` ->
  `engine.rs:693-695` (`"failed to execute fragment: {err}"`) is unchanged. Fix 2's `Err` arm
  (`engine.rs:291-316` today) sees the same `Err`, ~100 s earlier. Fix 2's design does not depend on when
  the `Err` arrives (its spec section 8 said so; fix 1 spec section 8 asked for exactly that).
- **Which siblings had parked when the Err lands is decided by queue order, not time.** The dispatch
  worker is one thread popping a FIFO (`compute_node_service.rs:380-391`, `mpsc::channel` at `:259`), so the
  senders ahead of q05's lineitem sender in the inbox had finished and parked (`slots=2`, measured in the
  campaign's wipe WARN) and the ones behind it had not, whether the sender dies after 100 s or 2.7 s. Fix 2's
  acceptance A4 (`q05 trigger=engine_err fragments=2 slots=2`) therefore holds under fix 1. Inference from
  the single-thread structure; the fix1+2 arm confirms it.
- **Fix 1's text becomes fix 2's `cause`.** The ~600-character reason string (fix 1 spec 3.1) is stored per
  retired query (`RetiredQueries`, 1024 entries), copied into each poisoned-slot message and into gate 4's
  `"query {q} already failed on this CN: {cause}"`. Size is irrelevant (< 1 MB worst case); fix 1's client
  greps (`gave up after`, `held outside any task reservation`, `freed 0 bytes`) still match because the
  failing fragment's own error is what the FE reports first; gate 4's wrapped text is only returned for
  late arrivals, which the FE ignores while cancelling (`DefaultCoordinator.java:1054-1057`, fix 2 spec 5.2).
- **Fix 1's `has_error()` early-out** (`gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:131-139` insertion) drops queued tasks of
  the failed query inside the engine; it never changes what `Fragment::run()` returns. No effect on fix 2.
- **Timing numbers that move.** Fix 2's arm C criterion C6 ("sweep wall shorter by ~11.9 s") was written
  against the campaign; with fix 1 in the build the sweep is ~745 s shorter for a different reason. Fix 1's
  arm A wall bounds (criterion 3) include leftover-fragment time that fix 2 removes (q17 -> q18 6.42 s,
  measured `E/agent-notes/refute-oom5/notes.md`). Both specs already made their primary criteria immune
  (fix 1: measured from the first OOM in the engine log; fix 2: `base@start` and per-id `fragment run
  started` counts). C6 is rewritten (section 7).
- **Landing-order contradiction resolved.** Fix 1 spec 8 says "land first"; fix 2 spec 10 said "land fix 2
  before fix 1's SF1000 time-to-fail arm". Both are satisfiable: code lands fix 1 then fix 2 (no shared
  files), fix 1's arm A/B run once on the fix-1 build for attribution, and fix 2's arm C on the fix1+2
  build re-measures the six (it is the report's before/after row). Fix 2 spec 10 edited accordingly.

### 2.2 Fix 1 vs fix 4a: fix 1 does not make a fused q21 die fast

The fusion spec (8, arm A; 10) assumed a fused q21 that OOMs "with fix 1 in the same build dies in
seconds". That holds only when the downgrade frees 0 bytes. Today's six die with `freed == 0` because a
`GPU_SCAN -> STREAMING_SINK` leaf registers no repository (`src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112`,
report B2). A fused F07 is a join fragment: its build-side partitions sit in inter-pipeline port
repositories (`repository_wiring_materializer.cpp:68-69`), which TIER 1 converts to HOST (160 GiB
configured, empty). So the reschedule path will see `freed > 0`, rule 5 keeps retrying, and q21 either
passes slowly through spilling or spends up to 100 retries x spill rounds before the cap. Which of the
two happens is not predictable from the evidence (report 5.10: spill throughput never measured). Consequences:

- Fusion arm A must record for q21: the `HASH_JOIN (id=10)` build port, the count of `after downgrade
  (N bytes freed)` lines with N > 0, `[host_pool]` growth, and time-to-fail or pass. It is a data point, not
  a pass criterion (fusion decision 1 already says q21 is recorded, not required).
- Fix 1's arm A bound ("one retry round after the first OOM") is a claim about today's plan shapes only.
  Fix 1 spec section 8 edited to say so.
- If q21 turns out to thrash (many rounds, each freeing a little), that is fix 4b's / the spill policy's
  problem, not a fix 1 regression: today q21 takes 114.5 s to die; fix 1 never makes anything slower.

### 2.3 Fix 2 vs fix 4a: the same two files, one semantic overlap

Verified anchors (`compute_node_service.rs`): `exec_single_attachment :705-717` calls
`try_dispatch_sender` (`:309-329`) **before** `process_fragment` (`:918-959`); `run_ready_fragment :864-911`
wraps `execute_ready_fragment :1325-1394`; `cancel_plan_fragment :457-479`. `local_exchange.rs`:
`SenderSource` enum `:26-48` with `names() :52-56` and `is_complete() :59-64`; `take_ready` removals `:282-308`.

| place | fix 2 | fix 4a | resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cancel_plan_fragment` | full teardown: `results.cancel_query`, `exchanges.retire_receiver(id)` -> `release_sources`, `executor.retire_query` (commit 2, 4.4g) | inserts `exchanges.forget_query(query_id)` (4.6) | **fix 2 owns it.** `retire_receiver` removes every `sources` entry of the cancelled receiver, which includes a deferred `LocalPlan`; a `LocalPlan` holds no GPU memory and no lease, so `release_sources` needs no arm for it (write the release as `if let SenderSource::Remote {..}` so a third variant compiles). Fusion 4.6 and `forget_query` are dropped; the fusion spec's own section 10 already offered this. |
| `execute_ready_fragment` | restructures: split `ready.inputs` before translation, `StagedLeases` RAII guard (4.4e) | prepends `fold_deferred_plans(ready)` returning `(params, streamed, fused)` (4.5) | fold first, then fix 2's split/guard over `streamed` and `&params`; `dump_fragment(&params)` dumps the fused plan. Pure sequencing; fusion rebases. |
| `run_ready_fragment` | gate 3 at the top: `failure_of(query_id)` -> `release_staged(ready.inputs)`, skip (4.4c) | fused receivers arrive here through `dispatch`/`dispatch_then_join` like any ready receiver | gate 3 covers fused receivers for free; `release_staged` sees a `LocalPlan` in `ready.inputs` and must ignore it (same `if let` rule). |
| `process_fragment` | gate 4 after the translate-only block, before `receiver_exchanges` (4.4d) | `try_defer_sender` hook after the receiver branch, before `translate_fragment_logged` (4.4) | gate 4 runs first on the inline and batch paths, so a dead query's leaf is refused before it can be deferred. |
| `try_dispatch_sender` (async path, the campaign setting) | untouched by fix 2 | hook after `resolve_descriptor_table`, before `dispatch` | **gap:** on the async path the fusion hook runs before any fix 2 gate. A leaf of a dead query would be deferred, the receiver readied, and only then skipped by gate 3 (no GPU work, but a misleading `fused sender fragment` INFO line and a needless `LocalPlan` clone). Fixed by adding a `failure_of` check as the first policy step of `try_defer_sender` (fusion spec 4.4 edited; fix 2 spec 10 asked for exactly this). |
| `SenderSource` | `release_staged`/`release_sources` iterate `Remote`; `retire_receiver` returns `Vec<SenderSource>` | adds `LocalPlan(LocalPlan)`; extends `names()`/`is_complete()` | additive; fix 2 writes its matches non-exhaustively. |
| `ExchangeState` | `retired: HashSet`, `retired_order`, `retire_receiver`, `is_retired` | `offer_local_plan`, (`forget_query` dropped) | disjoint methods on one struct; textual merge only. |
| `engine.rs` | rewritten around `ParkedRegistry` | not edited (fusion spec 4.8) | none. |
| `lib.rs` (CN) | `mod parked_registry;` | none (fusion adds `pub mod fusion;` to the **translator** crate's `lib.rs`) | none. |
| test fixtures | `Retiring<E>` wrapper; tests built on `propagation_chain :3311` (sinks are `data_stream_sink`, UNPARTITIONED, `:3806`) | `hash_partitioned_data_stream_sink`, `RecordingRunExecutor`, `FailingExecutor` (no name clash: today only `FailingIntermediateExecutor :2000`, `RecordingExecutor :2914`, `CountingExecutor :1810` exist) | fusion's `Tunables` default is `Leaf`, which fuses only `HASH_PARTITIONED` sinks, so every fix 2 test keeps parking. Rule for both: fix 2 tests never use a hash-partitioned single-destination local leaf unless they call `set_fragment_fusion(Off)`. |
| `DEMO.md:37-42` | new bullet under "What it does not exercise yet" | rewrites the "Sequential fragments" bullet at `:39-40` | adjacent lines: fusion rebases. |

Gate 1/gate 2 (engine thread) and the `RetireQuery` request are untouched by fusion. A fused receiver that
fails is attributed to the receiver's ids (fusion 4.8), so `fail_fragment` -> `retire_query` works
unchanged; a deferred sender never ran, so there is nothing of it for fix 2 to drop.

### 2.4 Fix 3 vs fix 4a: complementary, but fusion's goldens are for today's plans

- **Six at 1 CN.** Fix 3 predicts (Appendix B, inference re-derived by both judges) that the FE keeps
  hash-partitioning lineitem at 1 CN whenever the other side exceeds ~5M rows; the six keep the P1 shape and
  fusion still applies. If the prediction is wrong and lineitem ends up inside the join fragment, there is
  nothing to fuse and the query passes anyway.
